subject.title: Add testing framework for cron jobs and skills (dry-run mode)

question: What public guarantee should cron and skill testing provide: static validation only, execution up to the model boundary, or a full agent turn with universally intercepted tools and deliveries?
rationale: Those modes have materially different fidelity, security, concurrency, plugin compatibility, and CI semantics, so implementation cannot safely choose the boundary from the issue sketch alone.

options.title: Phased scoped contract
options.body: Ship request-scoped static cron validation and an explicit-input skill harness first, then add capability-aware execution interception after the shared tool contract is approved.

options.title: Full universal dry-run
options.body: Design one core run context that intercepts every tool, plugin hook, delivery, command job, and client tool, accepting the larger compatibility and security program.

options.title: Retain inspection only
options.body: Treat existing cron inspection and normal skill invocation as sufficient and decline a stronger no-side-effect execution guarantee.

recommendation.title: Phased scoped contract
recommendation.body: Ship request-scoped static cron validation and an explicit-input skill harness first, then add capability-aware execution interception after the shared tool contract is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the existing design review and have the broadest recent history across the affected cron, skills, and runtime boundaries.
